types.definition: The SEA objectives are to provide a high level of protection to the environment and contribute to integrating environmental considerations into the preparation, adoption and implementation of plans and programmes to promote sustainable development. It should include risk assessments. SEA applies to a wide range of public plans and programmes, including land use, transport, energy, waste, agriculture.

types.name: Assessment* of ecological limits
types.definition: research of impacts of biodiversity loss drivers on the ecosystem, the limits for the ecosystem and measures of how the drivers can be reduced research based on literature, key-experts, data-reviews, field studies or citizen science data Note: For more generic research see 2.04 Scientific Research, incl. 2.04.14 citizen science

types.name: Research and monitoring of the environmental conditions, potential impacts by the intervention and long-term consequences
types.definition: surveys, ex-ante and post assessments, community consultations, studies Note: For more generic research see 2.04 Scientific Research

types.name: Monitoring strategies and verification systems
types.definition: generating/providing adequate data, allow for effective control and basis to take counter-measures for people not obeying the law or corrective measures if the law/intervention has unintended effects in some countries Public order-related institutions need to authorize the access to high-level quality spatial data

types.name: Delineation and zoning
types.definition: Integrated landscape planning* and identification, mapping and description of land ownership and tenure for all properties relevant for current or potential conservation, planned land-use changes or other type of intervention that aims to halt biodiversity loss; realize an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)* before any type of land-use change Note: Delineation and zoning within PAs and ICCAs are within 7.01.02 Land protection planning (7 Protection and other conservation measures)
types.examples: may include costs for personnel or legal assistance, stakeholder* engagement and consultation, registry research, legal fees, field cadastral surveys, meetings, etc.

types.name: Urban planning, including e.g. green infrastructure development, ecosystem-based solutions*
types.definition: Integrated landscape planning*, e.g. dedicated green areas, planning for ecosystem services, "green" infrastructure, nature-based solutions* for services

types.name: Non-urban spatial planning
types.definition: Integrated landscape planning*, e.g. areas dedicated to protection, areas excluded for industrialization or agriculture, measures for rural livelihoods while supporting biodiversity
types.examples: may include costs for personnel or legal assistance, registry research, legal fees, field cadastral surveys, meetings, etc.

types.name: Marine spatial planning
types.definition: Integrated seascape planning* and mapping, description, and allocation of distribution, extent and intensity of marine use

types.name: Land tenure legislation and regulation of land ownership, including purchase of land
types.definition: Clarifying land rights, including historical and traditional claims by indigenous people, transfer development rights*, resolve land disputes, reducing ownership insecurity note: while in general clear land tenure rights provides the conditions to consider long-term measures (good for biodiversity), private ownership of land is no guarantee for owners effectively taking this measures
types.examples: Preparation, formulation, negotiation, adoption and implementation of laws, regulations, property purchase, may include actual property costs, personnel for negotiations, taxes, loan interest, boundary demarcation removal of hazardous conditions (e.g., toxic waste), etc.

types.name: Cross-border cooperation
types.definition: Measures at borders, cooperation and alignment of spatial planning along the borders

types.name: Ratification proccess for relevant conventions focusing directly on biodiversity: Convention on Biological Diversity and its protocols, Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals, The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA), Convention on Wetlands (Ramsar Convention), World Heritage Convention (WHC), High Seas Treaty, International Plant Protection Convention (IPPC), including regional conventions and those related to environmental rights (e.g. Aarhus Convention, Escazu Agreement)
types.definition: Sign and ratify the convention; participate in convention-related meetings, information exchange, national/ rights holders*/ stakeholder* consultation, create necessary institutions, adopt the relevant legislation accordingly Note: For the Nagoya protocol see specific subcategory in 1.04 For implementation see relevant subcategories

types.name: Ratification proccess for all other conventions, initiatives and alliances that either tackle biodiversity loss drivers or broader environmental objectives e.g. UNCLOS, any Pollution-related Convention, UNFCCC, etc
types.definition: Sign and ratify the convention; participate in convention-related meetings, information exchange, national/ rights holders*/ stakeholder* consultation, create necessary institutions, adopt the relevant legislation accordingly Note: For implementation see relevant subcategories

types.name: Gap analysis
types.definition: Check current law for potential gaps, necessary changes or new law in order to implement the convention Note: For the actual legal process of changing or introducing new law, refer to 5.01 BD laws or 5.02 Other relevant laws
types.examples: Research, studies

types.name: Institutionalization, monitoring and reporting
types.definition: Establish relevant bodies, institutions (and integrate them into the current system) or dedicate persons within existing governance institutions to monitor implementation, report (as required), create awareness
types.examples: preparation, setting-up and managing the relevant public bodies

types.name: Access to financial resources for Indigenous Peoples and local communities*, women, youth and other stakeholders*
types.examples: preparation, formulation, negotiation, adoption and implementation of laws, regulations and agreements; supporting indigenous organisation, providing materials, access to legal systems Note: ABS-specific benefit sharing mechanisms are in 1.03.03, related financial mechanisms in 1.03.04

types.name: Access to non-financial resources for Indigenous Peoples and local communities*, women, youth and other stakeholders*
types.examples: preparation, formulation, negotiation, adoption and implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, modifying distribution and accessibility regulations to technology, software, tools, etc, awareness raising

types.name: Access to information for Indigenous Peoples and local communities*, women, youth and other stakeholders*
types.examples: prepare/planning media campaigns, stakeholder* analysis, preparation of information materials, translation, complaint mechanism, responsible and accessible transparency teams

types.name: Access to decision-making for Indigenous Peoples and local communities*, women, youth and other stakeholders*
types.definition: Facilitation of the rights-holders* and stakeholders* participation for planning and implementation by informing accurately and comprehensivly about environmental and social impacts, provide space for their opinion, organize consultations, etc
types.examples: travel, meetings, information, translation, participant support

types.name: Establish national, regional and international contact points, plattforms and community facilitators
types.examples: preparation, setting-up and managing the relevant contact points and institutions

types.name: Implementation of relevant conventions
types.definition: e.g. Aarhus Convention, the Escazu Agreement (where applicable)
types.examples: sign and ratify the convention; participate in convention-related meetings, information exchange, adopt the relevant legislation accordingly, implement or scale up corresponding activities, monitor and evaluate the implementation of the commitments and adjust implementation as necessary

types.name: Identification and verification of pollution sources for soil, groundwater and surface water
types.definition: e.g. by doing national soil or water surveys and site investigations, including novel techniques like geographical information systems (GIS), remote sensing, visible and near infrared spectroscopy (Vis-NIR), nuclear and multi-isotopic techniques
types.examples: Includes information exchange at regional and global levels, desktop research, national and field surveys, regular measurements and sensors

types.name: Soil/ Water Pollution Management Plan
types.definition: including risk assessments, the incorporation of purposeful indicators* (e.g. water or soil quality, limits for specific pollutants) and relevant standards, planning of actions, reporting and monitoring*, and enforce implementation
types.examples: Planning, preparation, relevant research on baselines, define goals, measures, implement monitoring and evaluation, coordination among institutions and stakeholders*

types.name: Incentives and regulation to prevent soil and water pollution
types.definition: e.g. pollution limits or minimum quality standards for industrial processes, including wastewater management, incentives to change the production processes; Note: Specific measures to reduce nutrient excess from agriculture or aquaculture can be found in 9.02 or 9.03 within 9 Sustainable Use
types.examples: Planning, preparation, relevant research on baselines, exchange of information at different levels, define goals, measures, implement monitoring* and evaluation

types.name: Incentives and regulation to reduce eutrophication
types.definition: Besides reducing the drivers of eutrophication (see measures in this subcategory and improved waste management in 6.03), the focus here is on measures to reduce existing eutrophication, e.g. planting native species next to water areas, removing of dead plant material etc
types.examples: Includes the personal, travel, purchase of plants, planning, field visits and implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, related to irrigation and release of water

types.name: Incentives and regulation for (obligatory) impact assessments*, reporting, restoration of polluted sites and guaranteeing specific standards
types.definition: Frameworks for impact assessments, restoration of polluted sites and setting clear (regionalized) limits of pollutants, extended producer responsibility (EPR) along the whole product chain, regulatory/financial incentives for cleaner production (e.g. positive incentives in form of grants, permits, preferable purchasing agreements, tax deductions or depreciation allowances, and other favourable financial instruments or negative incentives as pollution permit fees, tax and/or fines or by using market-based approaches by creating a market for the pollution units and/or introducing taxes that aim to internalize the pollution costs for the society and/or introduce and implement fines for illegal pollution), aiming for less waste and pollution, more reused or recycled material, including incentives for a more sustainable design (lesser material, easy reparation, easier recyclable/ disposable) and production, contaminated sites management, and limit the use of certain products and other laws facilitating the implementation of the targeted soil/water quality standards
types.examples: Includes implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements,

types.name: Pollution permit fees, tax and/or fines
types.definition: e.g. market-based approaches as markets for the pollution units (legal right to pollute at a certain cost) and/or taxes that aim to internalize the pollution costs for the society and/or fines for illegal pollution
types.examples: Studies and evaluation to determine the amount; implementation and enforcement of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, Stakeholder consultation

types.name: Cleaning up of polluted soil, groundwater or surface water
types.definition: Using physical, chemical and biological measures, both in-situ or ex-situ cleaning (removal of contaminated soil), including soil decontamination at former industrial sites, landfills and other black spots, dredging of pollutants from water bodies (rivers, lakes, estuaries, etc.), the decontamination and cleaning up of surface water with e.g. disinfection, boiling, solar distillation, filtration, ozone water disinfection, activated charcoal absorption, and ultraviolet disinfection following accidental pollution e.g. through collection of pollutants or through application of chemicals, as well as the cleaning up of oil spills on land, inland surface waters and seas, including coastal areas Note: for emergency restoration measures after environmental accidents, see 8.02 Site redevelopment and engineering in 8 Restoration

types.name: Monitor* implementation and enforce existing law
types.definition: control with field studies, sensors, and other forms of measuring data to see the pollution reduction or compliance with law, focusing on mayor pollutant sources (agriculture, industry, waste) and by establishing and maintaining monitoring networks and assessment systems
types.examples: Includes generation of data, controls, field visits, enhance capability of criminal justice system

types.name: Implementation of relevant convention initiatives and alliances
types.definition: here especially the Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and other Matter (London Convention); the UN Treaty on Plastic Pollution and commitments agreed on at UNEA3 (relevant for all pollution subcategories), Note: for those agreements see also 6.04.10 Coastal and marine pollution or initiatives like the Global Soil Partnership
types.examples: Designation of National Focal Points (NFP)*, participation in convention-related meetings, information exchange, implement or scale up corresponding activities, consultations, monitor and evaluate the implementation of the commitments and adjust implementation as necessary

types.name: Identifying and verifying sources of pollution for ambient air and climate
types.definition: includes information exchange at regional and global levels, desktop research, national and field surveys, regular measurements and sensors E.g. by doing air pollution surveys and site investigations, including novel techniques like geographical information systems (GIS), remote sensing, nuclear and multi-isotopic techniques

types.name: Air Pollution Management Plan, and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)
types.definition: need to include biodiversity consideration in the plan, including risk assessments*, the incorporation of purposeful indicators* (e.g. air quality, limits for specific pollutants) and relevant standards, planning of actions, reporting and monitoring*, and enforce implementation
types.examples: Planning, preparation, relevant research on baselines, exchange of information at different levels, define goals, measures, implement monitoring and evaluation

types.name: Incentives to prevent pollution through in-process modifications (cleaner technologies and/or use of cleaner products) for those modifications
types.definition: Measures ensuring that air pollutants are eliminated or reduced by cleaner technologies, that replaces existing production process during production, storage and/or transportation or by modified facilities that allows a substitution of raw materials, energy, catalysts and other inputs by non- (or less) polluting products, or of treating raw materials prior to their use in order to make them less polluting
types.examples: includes implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, as well as planning and implement the subsidy

types.name: Incentives and regulation for the treatment of exhaust gases and ventilation air
types.definition: Activities involving the installation, maintenance and operation of end-of-pipe equipment for the removal and reduction of emissions of particulate matter or other air-polluting substances either from the combustion of fuels or from processes: filters, dedusting equipment, catalytic converters, post-combustion and other techniques. Also included are activities aimed at increasing the dispersion of gases so as to reduce concentrations of air pollutants

types.name: Incentives and regulation, to reduce emission of CO2 and similar climate-damaging gases
types.definition: Related to measures the private sector can take (in particular extractive industries, energy, construction and transportation) and related legislation; or by providing sustainable consumer choices (e.g. more public transport, recycling and repairing facilities, etc)
types.examples: includes implementation of legislations, incentives, rural/urban planning, carbon reduction schemes

types.name: Incentives and regulation, to reduce the emission of nitrogen through changes in farming and raising animals
types.definition: For feeding: without unnecessary N and P-surpluses, according to life cycle and productivity of the animals (multi-phase feeding). For manure and slurry: Slurry tank and manure stores are covered by solid lids, plastic sheeting or natural crust, depending on the type of manure; solid manure is stored on solid level ground in a dry/covered location. Manure and slurry is only applied at the appropriate time (storage needs to have sufficient capacity)
types.examples: includes implementation of legislation and incentives

types.name: Incentives and regulation to reduce sulphur and nitrogen emissions and ground level ozone*
types.definition: Ground level ozone, also called Tropospheric ozone formed with a chemical reaction of oxides of nitrogen (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOC) in presence of heat and light. E.g. by reducing ship emissions, in particular sulphur and nitrogen, car and other transport emissions, power plants, industrial boilers, refineries emissions
types.examples: includes implementation of legislation and incentives

types.name: Incentives and regulation for (obligatory) impact assessments*, reporting, restoration of polluted sites and guaranteeing specific standards, including positive and negative incentives
types.definition: Frameworks for impact assessments, restoration of polluted sites and setting clear (regionalized) limits of pollutants, extended producer responsibility (EPR) along the whole product chain, regulatory/financial incentives for cleaner production (e.g. positive incentives in form of grants, permits, preferable purchasing agreements, tax deductions or depreciation allowances, and other favourable financial instruments or negative incentives as pollution permit fees, tax and/or fines or by using market-based approaches by creating a market for the pollution units and/or introducing taxes that aim to internalize the pollution costs for the society and/or introduce and implement fines for illegal pollution), aiming for less waste and pollution, more reused or recycled material, including incentives for a more sustainable design (lesser material, easy reparation, easier recyclable/ disposable) and production, contaminated sites management, and limit the use of certain products and other laws facilitating the implementation of the targeted soil/water quality standards
types.examples: Includes implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements

types.name: Pollution permit fees, tax and/or fines
types.definition: e.g. market-based approaches as markets for the pollution units (legal right to pollute at a certain cost) and/or taxes that aim to internalize the pollution costs for the society and/or fines for illegal pollution
types.examples: Studies and evaluation to determine the amount; implementation and enforcement of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, Stakeholder consultation

types.name: Phasing out of depleting substances of the ozone layer
types.definition: Implement and enforcing corresponding legislation, support for using alternatives
types.examples: includes implementation of legislation and incentives

types.name: Clean air to reduce pollution
types.definition: Processes and measures that clean the air using physical (e.g. filtering), biological (e.g. plants) or chemical methods (neutralizing contaminants)

types.name: Monitoring* of pollution levels and air quality
types.definition: control with field studies, sensors, and other forms of measuring data to see the pollution reduction or compliance with law, focusing on mayor pollutant sources (agriculture, industry, waste) and by establishing and maintaining monitoring networks and assessment systems
types.examples: includes generation of data, controls, field visits, enhance capability of criminal justice system

types.name: Implementation of relevant conventions initiatives, and alliances
types.definition: here the Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution (CLRTAP) and commitments agreed on at UNEA3 (relevant for all pollution subcategories) or initiatives like the Climate and Clean Air Coalition to Reduce Short-lived Climate Pollutants and the Global Methane Initiative
types.examples: Designation of National Focal Points (NFP)*, participation in convention-related meetings, information exchange, implement or scale up corresponding activities, consultations, monitor and evaluate the implementation of the commitments and adjust implementation as necessary

types.name: Development and implementation of a waste strategy
types.definition: including risk assessments*, environmental impact assessments*, incorporating relevant standards, planning of actions, reporting and monitoring*, and enforce implementation
types.examples: Planning, preparation, relevant research on baselines, define goals, measures, implement monitoring and evaluation

types.name: Incentives and regulation to prevent of solid, industrial, medical, hazardous, toxic, etc waste and wastewater
types.definition: e.g. by incentivizing or regulating measures that towards a circular economy, change of resources, design of the product and processes, improved reusing and recycling, replacing material, in-house modification
types.examples: includes implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements

types.name: Incentives and regulation for (required) labelling and access to relevant and accurate information for consumers, improving traceability
types.definition: focus on improving the traceability, easing the recovery and recycling of plastic material and other waste*, enable sustainable consumer choice
types.examples: includes implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements

types.name: Infrastructure and sites for reusing or recycling waste
types.definition: includes planning when biodiversity is concerned (e.g. Environmental Impact Assessments EIA*)
types.examples: includes construction, maintenance, operational cost, studies

types.name: Collection, treatment and disposal of household, commercial and industrial waste
types.definition: The household, commercial and industrial waste management (including hazardous waste* and wastewater treatment*) includes its mechanical, biological and/or thermal treatment (beyond recycling, considered in 6.03.04), in order to neutralise it, render it non-hazardous, safer for transport, amenable for recovery or storage, or to reduce it in volume (minimisation of waste as such is part of 6.03.02) includes also maintenance costs for the facilities (e.g. septic tanks for wastewater)

types.name: Sewage* networks and infrastructure
types.definition: Activities aimed at the operation of sewerage networks, i.e. the collection and transport of wastewater* from one or several users, as well as rainwater, by means of sewerage networks, collectors, tanks and other means of transport (sewage vehicles, etc.), including maintenance and repair.

types.name: Wastewater* treatment
types.definition: Removal of impurities and contaminants by physical (e.g. sedimentation, flotation), biological (with aerobic or anaerobic micro-organisms) or chemical treatments or advanced technologies (e.g. chemical coagulation, flocculation and precipitation; break-point chlorinating; stripping; mixed media filtration; micro-screening; selective ion exchange; activated carbon absorption; reverse osmosis; ultra-filtration; elector flotation).

types.name: Economic incentives for civil society
types.definition: Measures include waste* fees, fines, taxes in particular for landfill and incineration (or similar with the intent to internalize environmental costs), deposit-refund schemes, tradable permits and subsidies
types.examples: includes preparation, planning and implementation of the incentives

types.name: Incentives and regulation, or legislation for (obligatory) impact assessments*, reporting, trade policies, guaranteeing specific standards, including positive and negative incentives
types.definition: Frameworks for impact assessments, restoration of polluted sites and setting clear (regionalized) limits of pollutants, regulatory/financial incentives for cleaner production (e.g. positive incentives in form of grants, permits, preferable purchasing agreements, tax deductions or depreciation allowances, and other favourable financial instruments or negative incentives as pollution permit fees, tax and/or fines or by using market-based approaches by creating a market for the pollution units and/or introducing taxes that aim to internalize the pollution costs for the society and/or introduce and implement fines for illegal pollution), extended producer responsibility (EPR) along the whole product chain, aiming for less waste* and pollution, more reused or recycled material, including incentives for a more sustainable design (lesser material, easy reparation, easier recyclable/ disposable) and production, contaminated sites management, and limit the use of certain products and other laws facilitating the implementation of the targeted soil/water quality standards
types.examples: includes implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements

types.examples: Studies and evaluation to determine the amount; implementation and enforcement of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, Stakeholder consultation

types.name: Monitoring* of waste and its environmental consequences
types.definition: control with field studies, sensors, and other forms of measuring data to see the pollution reduction or compliance with law, focusing on mayor pollutant sources (agriculture, industry, waste*) and by establishing and maintaining monitoring networks and assessment systems
types.examples: includes generation of data, controls, field visits, enhance capability of criminal justice system

types.name: Implementation of relevant conventions
types.definition: here related to the Basel Convention (Hazardous Wastes), the Rotterdam Convention on the Prior Informed Consent Procedure for Certain Hazardous and commitments agreed on at UNEA3 (for Basel and Rotterdam, see also 6.04.10 Coastal and marine pollution; UNEA3 relevant for all pollution subcategories)
types.examples: Designation of National Focal Points (NFP)*, participation in convention-related meetings, information exchange, implement or scale up corresponding activities, consultations, monitor and evaluate the implementation of the commitments and adjust implementation as necessary

types.definition: e.g. by doing water and coastal surveys and site investigations, including novel techniques like geographical information systems (GIS), remote sensing, visible and near infrared spectroscopy (Vis-NIR), nuclear and multi-isotopic techniques includes information exchange at regional and global levels, desktop research, national and field surveys, regular measurements and sensors,

types.name: Marine Debris Action/ Management Plan
types.definition: including risk assessments*, the incorporation of purposeful indicators* (e.g. water quality, limits for specific pollutants) and relevant standards, planning of actions, reporting and monitoring*, and enforce implementation
types.examples: Planning, preparation, relevant research on baselines, exchange of information at different levels, define goals, measures, implement monitoring and evaluation

types.name: Incentives and regulation preventing and reducing ocean acidification
types.definition: policies should include measures like reduction of CO2 emissions (regulations/incentives for measures by the private sector or state-owned companies, in particular extractive industries, energy, construction and transportation and providing options for sustainable consumer choices) and related legislation;
types.examples: includes implementation of legislations, rural/urban planning,

types.name: Incentives and regulation reducing the plastic debris in water
types.definition: policies should include measures like phasing out specific plastic products, extended producer responsibility (EPR) along the whole product chain, measures related to ships (measures related to oil, chemical, lost cargo, sewage, garbage), etc includes preparation, formulation, negotiation, adoption and implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements

types.name: Incentives and regulation for (obligatory) impact assessments*, reporting, trade policies restoration of polluted sites and guaranteeing specific standards, including positive and negative incentives
types.definition: Frameworks for impact assessments, restoration of polluted sites and setting clear (regionalized) limits of pollutants, regulatory/financial incentives for cleaner production (e.g. positive incentives in form of grants, permits, preferable purchasing agreements, tax deductions or depreciation allowances, and other favourable financial instruments or negative incentives as pollution permit fees, tax and/or fines or by using market-based approaches by creating a market for the pollution units and/or introducing taxes that aim to internalize the pollution costs for the society and/or introduce and implement fines for illegal pollution), extended producer responsibility (EPR) along the whole product chainaiming for less waste and pollution, more reused or recycled material, including incentives for a more sustainable design (lesser material, easy reparation, easier recyclable/ disposable) and production, contaminated sites management, and limit the use of certain products and other laws facilitating the implementation of the targeted soil/water quality standards
types.examples: includes implementation of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, as well as planning and implement financial subsidies

types.definition: e.g. market-based approaches as markets for the pollution units (legal right to pollute at a certain cost) and/or taxes that aim to internalize the pollution costs for the society and/or fines for illegal pollution
types.examples: Studies and evaluation to determine the amount; implementation and enforcement of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, Stakeholder consultation

types.name: Monitoring* of litter and plastics (micro & macro)
types.definition: Monitor and analyse in order to coordinate marine litter action, share and establish data collection frameworks and contribute to (large-scale) data repositories/portals, using traditional field techniques and/or digital means as satellites, drones or sensors.

types.name: Cleaning up beaches and coastal area
types.definition: Removing plastic and other waste before entering into the water course, as well as cases in environmental courts* against polluters and the enforcement of verdicts in such cases

types.name: Cleaning up after ship accidents or infrastructure failure (e.g. oil spills)
types.definition: including physical, chemical or biological means of cleaning, as well as cases in environmental courts* against polluters and the enforcement of verdicts in such cases

types.name: Implementation of relevant conventions
types.definition: here especially the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS - see also 7.03.06 OECMs, 09.04.07 Sustainable Fisheries), IMO Ballast Water Management (BWM - see also 3.01.11 Invasive Alien Species and 9.04.07 Sustainable Fisheries), UN Treaty on Plastic Pollution, Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and other Matter (London Convention) (for Plastic and London see also 6.01.09 Soil, groundwater and surface water), as well as Basel Convention (Hazardous Wastes), the Rotterdam Convention on the Prior Informed Consent Procedure for Certain Hazardous (for Basel and Rotterdam, see also 6.03.12 Waste management), the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs), International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution of the Sea by Oil, International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL - see also 9.04.07 see also Sustainable Fisheries), International Convention on Oil Pollution Preparedness, Response and Cooperation (OPRC), or any of the relevant regional action plans on Marine Litter and commitments agreed on at UNEA3 (Note: relevant for all pollution subcategories)
types.examples: Designation of National Focal Points (NFP)*, participation in convention-related meetings, information exchange, implement or scale up corresponding activities, consultations, monitor and evaluate the implementation of the commitments and adjust implementation as necessary

types.name: Identification, verification and prioritization of other types of pollution and most effective measures to address the pollution.
types.definition: Refers to all sources of pollution not yet covered in the section 6.01-6.04. The identification and verification can be done by both desktop review, surveys, field investigations, or by using novel techniques like geographical information systems (GIS), remote sensing, visible and near infrared spectroscopy (Vis-NIR), nuclear and multi-isotopic techniques. For the prioritization, the local and most effected persons should be effectively included.

types.name: Pollution or Pollutant Management Plan
types.definition: including risk assessments*, the incorporation of purposeful indicators* (e.g. limits for specific pollutants) and relevant standards, planning of actions, reporting and monitoring*, and enforce implementation
types.examples: Planning, preparation, relevant research on baselines, exchange of information at different levels, define goals, measures, implement monitoring and evaluation

types.name: Incentives and regulation, for prevention, reduction and treatment of other pollution, in particular noise* and vibration, light*, water temperature alteration
types.definition: Noise and vibration abatement refers to measures and activities aimed at the control, reduction and abatement of industrial and transport noise (on land and in water) and vibration. Activities for the abatement of neighbourhood noise (soundproofing of dancing halls, etc.) as well as activities for the abatement of noise in places frequented by the public (swimming pools, etc.), in schools, etc., are included (noise/ vibration reduction at work is excluded) Light pollution prevention and reduction includes the change to LED light sources, changes in the illumination of towns and streets such as reducing intensity and frequency, automatic sensor to dim or turn on/off light, adaption of the light scattering Processes which are used to treat cooling water by removing heat, e.g. by air cooling, cooling towers, cooling circuits, to meet applicable environmental standards before releasing it into the environment (e.g. rivers)

types.name: Incentives and regulation for prevention, reduction and treatment of other pollution, i.e. radiation
types.definition: Protection against radiation refers to activities and measures aimed at the reduction or elimination of the negative consequences of radiation emitted from any source. Included is the handling, transportation and treatment of high level radioactive waste, i.e. waste that, because of its high radionuclide content, requires shielding during normal handling and transportation.

types.name: Incentives and regulation for prevention and reduction of pharmaceutical pollution
types.definition: Protection against pharmaceutical pollution refers to activities and measures that ensure an reduction of disposing pharmacies in the environment, i.e. by establishing legislation and providing the facilities to ensure the correct disposal. Note: For additional measures as new, less biodiversity harmful design of medicines see Prevention of Waste (6.03.02) and improved Wastewater Treatment (6.03.07)

types.name: Incentives and regulation for prevention and reduction of pollution by heavy metals, e.g. mercury or lead; POPs*, and PCB
types.definition: Measures includes legislation that limits certain pollutants, e.g. phasing out lead in paint, mercury or remove the use of certain products, including PCB, the research for alternative production measures or inputs, (disposal is part of 6.03 Waste Management), identify and label equipment accordingly, ensure sound maintenance joining and implementing relevant conventions at Multilateral Environment Agreement (MEA), here for the Minamata Convention on Mercury, the Stockholm Convention or all measures mentioned within the convention

types.name: Pollution permit fees, tax and/or fines
types.definition: e.g. market-based approaches as markets for the pollution units (legal right to pollute at a certain cost) and/or taxes that aim to internalize the pollution costs for the society and/or fines for illegal pollution
types.examples: Studies and evaluation to determine the amount; implementation and enforcement of laws, regulations and other binding agreements, Stakeholder consultation

types.name: Assessments*, Monitoring* and Evaluations, as e.g. Impact and Strategic assessments (ex-ante or post), rapid ecological assessments, period and long-term reviews
types.definition: for each of the pollutions mentioned in this section 6.05
types.examples: includes research based on literature, key-experts, data-reviews, citizen-science data, examination of samples in laboratories, sensors, and other forms of measuring data to see the pollution reduction or compliance with law

types.name: Monitor implementation and enforce existing law
types.definition: control pollution reduction or compliance with law, by establishing and maintaining monitoring* networks and assessment systems
types.examples: includes studies, stakeholder* engagement, enhance capability of criminal justice system (staffing, capacity-building*, etc)

types.name: Risk assessments*, including the assessment of ecological limits
types.definition: focusing on reaching ecological limits, and the potential of hazards, the areas exposure to pollution or an accident and the vulnerability of the ecosystem Note: Risk frameworks and their mitigation are part of 2.04.06 in 2.04 Scientific Research (2 BD Awareness - Knowledge)
types.examples: research based on literature, key-experts, data-reviews, field studies or citizen science data

types.name: Awareness raising and outreach to general public to avoid pollution
types.definition: Part of communication, education and awareness (CEPA)* efforts, incl. campaigns, via product design, publicity, in public buildings and areas Note: for general Awareness Raising see Category 2 Awareness - Knowledge
types.examples: prepare/planning media campaigns, stakeholder* analysis, preparation of information materials, libraries, museums, excursion, advertisement

types.name: Lifelong learning, technical training & capacity-building* to reduce pollution harmful for biodiversity and about biodiversity friendly alternatives
types.definition: Note: For details related to learning and trainings OR if topics are broader, see 2.02 informal education (2.02.04 and 2.02.05)
types.examples: travel, venue, training material, workshop facilitator, translations

types.name: Research on alternative practices and materials that put less pressure on biodiversity or increase biodiversity
types.definition: focus on alternative materials and waste* prevention based on literature, key-experts, laboratories, experiments, data-reviews and field studies Note: For more generic research see 2.04 Scientific Research; incl. 2.04.12 citizen science

types.name: Exchange of information, data, best practices
types.definition: Includes all forms of South-South or Triangular learning and exchange of data, participation at conferences and events.

types.definition: Primary conservation areas are refers to areas that may meet all elements of the IUCN definition of a protected area, but which are not officially designated as such because the governance authority does not want the area to be recognised or reported as a protected area. Examples are areas managed by indigenous or local communities. Secondary and ancillary have biodiversity secondary as secondary conservation measures have the biodiversity only as secondary or unintended effect.

types.name: Establishment and maintenance of corridors
types.definition: Corridors are a way to maintain vital ecological or environmental connectivity by maintaining physical linkages between core areas. They are areas of suitable habitat, or habitat undergoing restoration, linking two or more protected areas (or linking important habitat that is not protected) to allow interchange of species, migration, gene exchange, etc. The area connects habitat of wildlife populations separated by human activities or structures (such as roads, development, or logging). This allows an exchange of individuals between populations, which may help prevent the negative effects of inbreeding and reduced genetic diversity (via genetic drift) that often occur within isolated populations. Corridors may also help facilitate the re-establishment of populations that have been reduced or eliminated due to random events (such as fires or disease).
